title: Why Do Planes Fly So High?

scenes.title: Why Do Planes Fly So High?
scenes.text: Big airliners cruise about eleven kilometers up. That's higher than Mount Everest! But why do they fly so high?

scenes.title: Thin Air
scenes.text: The higher you go, the thinner the air gets. Up at cruising height, there's only about a third as much air, so there's much less drag pushing against the plane.

scenes.title: Saving Fuel
scenes.text: Less drag means the engines don't have to work as hard. So the plane burns less fuel, and can fly much farther.

scenes.title: Above the Weather
scenes.text: Flying high also keeps the plane above most of the weather. Storms and bumpy clouds stay far below, so the ride is smoother.

scenes.title: Room to Spare
scenes.text: Height also means safety. Mountains are far below, and if anything goes wrong, the pilots have lots of time and space to fix it.

scenes.title: The Catch
scenes.text: But there's a catch. The air up there is too thin to breathe, and freezing cold, around minus fifty degrees! So warm air is pumped into the cabin, keeping everyone comfy inside.

scenes.title: Remember!
scenes.text: Thin air, less drag, less fuel, smoother rides, and lots of safety. That's why planes fly so high! See you on the next flight.
